chapters.title: A New Practice for a New Reality
chapters.sourcePressure: Modern knowledge work creates boundaryless overload because unfinished commitments stay mentally active as open loops until they are captured, clarified, and held in a trusted system.
chapters.coreMove: Spot overload as undefined open loops and move one live commitment into a trusted place with a next physical action.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating GTD as a calmer to-do list or generic stress advice instead of a specific handoff from memory to trusted external control.

chapters.title: Getting Control of Your Life: The Five Stages of Mastering Workflow
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter lays out the workflow sequence: capture, clarify, organize, reflect, and engage, with actionable items sorted into do, delegate, or defer and non-actionable items into trash, incubate, or reference.
chapters.coreMove: Run each incoming item through the five workflow stages before trusting your choice of what to do.
chapters.commonMisread: Memorizing five verbs as productivity vocabulary without showing the handoff from mixed stuff to defined options.

chapters.title: Getting Projects Creatively Under Way: The Five Phases of Project Planning
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter teaches natural project planning through purpose and principles, outcome visioning, brainstorming, organizing, and next actions, with a simple dining-out example as supported illustration.
chapters.coreMove: Move a project from vague intention through purpose, outcome, raw ideas, structure, and one next physical action.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning planning into a polished project plan before the purpose, desired outcome, and next move are clear.

chapters.title: Getting Started: Setting Up the Time, Space, and Tools
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter moves from theory to operating conditions: enough time, space, and simple tools must be ready so capture and review are easier than informal memory.
chapters.coreMove: Set up the physical and digital conditions that make capturing and clarifying commitments friction-light.
chapters.commonMisread: Shopping for an elaborate productivity tool instead of preparing the few conditions that let the system be used daily.

chapters.title: Collection: Corralling Your Stuff
chapters.sourcePressure: Collection is a full sweep of physical and mental incompletes, not selective note-taking, so loose material stops distracting attention from outside the system.
chapters.coreMove: Sweep every loose piece of stuff into visible capture points before deciding what any of it means.
chapters.commonMisread: Capturing only important-looking tasks and leaving small scraps, objects, and mental loops outside the system.

chapters.title: Processing: Getting "In" to Empty
chapters.sourcePressure: Processing means clarifying each collected item one at a time, deciding whether it is actionable, and moving the in-basket toward empty through decisions.
chapters.coreMove: Take one captured item at a time and decide what it is, whether it is actionable, and where it goes next.
chapters.commonMisread: Reviewing the in-basket repeatedly as if looking at items counts as deciding them.

chapters.title: Organizing: Setting Up the Right Buckets
chapters.sourcePressure: After clarification, each item needs a stable container so decisions do not collapse back into one mixed pile.
chapters.coreMove: Place each clarified item into the bucket where it can be found and acted on later.
chapters.commonMisread: Building a pretty taxonomy while clarified commitments still compete in one undifferentiated list.

chapters.title: Reviewing: Keeping Your System Functional
chapters.sourcePressure: Organized buckets become stale unless a regular review refreshes lists, projects, waiting-fors, and calendars so the system still matches reality.
chapters.coreMove: Refresh the whole system often enough that the lists regain credibility before you choose from them.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating review as inspirational reflection instead of maintenance that restores trust in concrete lists.

chapters.title: Doing: Making the Best Action Choices
chapters.sourcePressure: Once the system is current, action choice depends on context, time, energy, and priority, with the six horizons available as higher-level framing.
chapters.coreMove: Choose the next action by filtering the trusted list through where you are, how much time you have, your energy, and real priority.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming the most important item always comes first, regardless of context, available time, or energy.

chapters.title: Getting Projects Under Control
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter returns to project-level control after the daily ground game is reliable, using creative planning and project visibility without replaying the whole planning theory.
chapters.coreMove: Lift from next-action execution to project control by checking each project for a clear outcome, visible moving parts, and a next action.
chapters.commonMisread: Reopening every project as a grand planning exercise instead of using ground-level control to recover project visibility.

chapters.title: The Power of the Collection Habit
chapters.sourcePressure: This principles chapter explains why the habit of collecting open loops clears commitments out of the head and reduces psychic drag.
chapters.coreMove: Capture each open loop at the moment it appears so your mind stops rehearsing it as a substitute for control.
chapters.commonMisread: Repeating the mechanics of Chapter 5 instead of showing why capture itself changes mental load.

chapters.title: The Power of the Next-Action Decision
chapters.sourcePressure: This principles chapter explains why deciding the concrete next action reduces stuckness and changes how people engage with commitments.
chapters.coreMove: Turn each vague commitment into the next visible physical action so engagement becomes possible.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating next action as a motivational slogan rather than a concrete decision about the body’s next move.

chapters.title: The Power of Outcome Focusing
chapters.sourcePressure: This principles chapter explains why a clear desired result gives direction to action and planning, acting as a force multiplier for lower-level control.
chapters.coreMove: Name the desired outcome clearly enough that actions can be tested against what done should look like.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating outcome focusing as vision-board optimism instead of a practical standard for choosing and aligning next actions.
